headline: AI Slop, Age-Smart Guidance and the Screen-Time Reset
thesis: Fake AI-generated papers under real professors' names test academic trust, as Harvard offers age-based AI guidance and federal officials shift the screen-time debate from minutes to meaningful use.
summary: Inside Higher Ed reports that little-known journals have published "AI slop" papers under prominent academics' names, including Stanford's Jure Leskovec, without their knowledge. A day earlier it covered Harvard's new AI Guidance by Age matrix, built from 5,000+ studies. In K-12, EdTech Magazine covers a Department of Education Dear Colleague letter on screen time that focuses on quality of use, not minutes, and a 464-signer letter urging Congress to protect E-Rate. Campuses are still dealing with the Vanderbilt ransomware claim, while Ed-Fi's new API v8.1 and fall roadmap push interoperability forward.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 13, 2026 · Built from search results only; several sources (ISTE, Brookings, THE Journal, Education Technology Insights, EdTech Week) had no items dated this week, so recent or evergreen items are shown.

themes.title: Research & Academic Integrity
themes.body: Journals publishing AI-written papers under real scholars' names and AI peer reviews that beat humans are forcing new questions about scholarly trust.

themes.title: Screen Time & Purposeful Tech

themes.title: Connectivity & Funding

themes.title: Campus & School Cybersecurity

themes.title: Data & Interoperability
